content.description: Full GDScript content to write to the file

tool_description: Create a new Godot scene (.tscn) file with nodes. Use this to create player scenes, UI screens, game objects, etc.

root_node_name.description: Name of root node (default: derived from filename)

root_node_type.description: Type of root node (e.g., Node2D, CharacterBody2D, Control, Node3D). REQUIRED.

items.description: A node spec: {name|node_name, type|node_type, properties?, script?, groups?, children?}. Unknown keys are rejected with an error.

nodes.description: Array of child nodes to add. Each node spec: {name|node_name, type|node_type, properties?, script?, groups?, children?}. Use either {name, type} or the same {node_name, node_type} keys used at the top level — both work. Unknown keys (e.g. "class", "kind", "parent") return an error instead of silently producing a generic Node.

attach_script.description: Optional script path to attach to root node (res://path/to/script.gd)

tool_description: Read and parse a scene file to get its full node structure and properties. Use this to understand a scene before editing.

include_properties.description: Include node properties in the output (default: false)

tool_description: Add a node to an existing scene file. Supports an optional script attachment, group memberships, and a tree of children created in the same call (1 tool call instead of N). Children format: {name|node_name, type|node_type, properties?, script?, groups?, children?}. Both key styles are accepted so children can reuse the same keys you use at the top level (node_name, node_type) or the shorter form (name, type). Unknown child keys are rejected with a clear error.

node_type.description: Type of node (e.g., Sprite2D, Camera2D, RigidBody2D, CollisionShape2D)

parent_path.description: Path to parent node (. for root, or relative path like Sprite2D)

properties.description: Optional dictionary of properties to set on the node

script.description: Optional script path to attach to the new node (res://path/to/script.gd)

groups.description: Optional list of node groups this node should belong to. Persisted to the .tscn file.

children.description: Optional tree of children to create under the new node. Each entry has the same shape as add_node's args (minus parent_path). Use this to build sub-trees in one call.

tool_description: Remove a node from an existing scene file.

node_path.description: Path to the node to remove (cannot be root, use relative path)

tool_description: Modify a single property on a node in a .tscn scene file. For multiple properties at once use set_node_properties. ALWAYS use a tool to modify .tscn files — NEVER edit them as text. To attach or change a script, use attach_script (NOT modify_node_property with property="script") — modify_node_property only rewrites the .tscn on disk, leaving the editor's in-memory node without the script, which makes connect_signal fail.

node_path.description: Path to the node (. for root, or relative path like "Sprite2D")

property_name.description: Name of the property to modify (position, scale, rotation, modulate, visible, etc.)

value.description: New value for the property. ANY JSON value accepted: primitives (numbers, strings, booleans, null), arrays, or objects. Use the {type, ...} discriminated form for Godot variant types. Common forms: numeric (e.g. 1.5), boolean (true), string ("hello"), Vector2 ({type:"Vector2",x,y}), Vector3 ({type:"Vector3",x,y,z}), Color ({type:"Color",r,g,b,a}), Quaternion ({type:"Quaternion",x,y,z,w}), Basis ({type:"Basis",euler:{x,y,z}}), Transform3D ({type:"Transform3D",basis:{...},origin:{x,y,z}}), AABB ({type:"AABB",position:{x,y,z},size:{x,y,z}}), Rect2 ({type:"Rect2",x,y,width,height}), NodePath (string starting with "."). For Resource-typed properties (Texture2D, Mesh, Material, Shape, etc.) DO NOT pass values here — use set_resource_property, set_sprite_texture, set_mesh, set_material, or set_collision_shape.

tool_description: Rename a node in a scene.

node_path.description: Path to the node to rename

tool_description: Move a node to a different parent in a scene and optionally control its position among siblings.

node_path.description: Path to the node to move

new_parent_path.description: Path to the new parent node (. for root)

sibling_index.description: Optional position among siblings (0 = first child). Omit or -1 to append.

tool_description: Attach or change a script on a node in a scene.

node_path.description: Path to the node (. for root, or relative path)

tool_description: Remove a script from a node in a scene.

node_path.description: Path to the node (. for root)

tool_description: Create and assign a collision shape resource to a CollisionShape2D or CollisionShape3D node. Supports: CircleShape2D, RectangleShape2D, CapsuleShape2D, SphereShape3D, BoxShape3D, etc.

shape_type.description: Shape type: CircleShape2D, RectangleShape2D, CapsuleShape2D, SphereShape3D, BoxShape3D, etc.

shape_params.description: Shape parameters: {radius: 32} for circles, {size: {x: 64, y: 64}} for rectangles, etc.

tool_description:
Assign a texture resource to a Sprite2D / Sprite3D / TextureRect node in a .tscn scene file. Modes:
  • FromPath  — load any texture file from disk (png/jpg/webp/svg/.tres) via load(). Returns whatever Texture2D the importer produced (usually CompressedTexture2D). Most common after generate_2d_asset.
  • ImageTexture (DEPRECATED ALIAS for FromPath, kept for back-compat)
  • NewImageTexture — force-create an ImageTexture (in-memory) from a raw image file.
  • PlaceholderTexture2D — in-scene placeholder of a given size.
  • GradientTexture2D / NoiseTexture2D — procedural textures.
Response always includes texture_class (the actual Godot class the texture decoded to), width, height, and texture_path so the agent can confirm what landed without an extra get_resource_info call.

texture_type.description: How to obtain the texture. Prefer FromPath for assets on disk.

texture_params.description: Texture parameters. FromPath / ImageTexture / NewImageTexture: {path: "res://assets/sprite.png"}. PlaceholderTexture2D: {size: {x: 64, y: 64}}. GradientTexture2D / NoiseTexture2D: {width, height}.

tool_description: Add an instance of another scene (.tscn) as a child node. This is how you compose scenes from reusable parts (like prefabs). The instance maintains a live reference to the source scene. Use this instead of add_node when you want to reuse an existing scene.

scene_path.description: Path to the scene file being edited (the parent scene)

instance_path.description: Path to the .tscn scene to instance (the child/prefab scene)

node_name.description: Optional name for the instance. If omitted, uses the instanced scene's root node name.

parent_path.description: Path to parent node within the scene (. for root, or relative path like Level/Enemies)

properties.description: Optional property overrides on the instance root (e.g., {position: {type: "Vector3", x: 5, y: 0, z: 10}})

tool_description: Create and assign a mesh resource to a MeshInstance3D node. REQUIRED to make 3D geometry visible. Primitive types: BoxMesh, SphereMesh, CylinderMesh, CapsuleMesh, PlaneMesh, PrismMesh, TorusMesh, QuadMesh, TextMesh. Or load from file.

node_path.description: Path to the MeshInstance3D node within the scene

mesh_type.description: Mesh class: "BoxMesh", "SphereMesh", "CylinderMesh", "CapsuleMesh", "PlaneMesh", "PrismMesh", "TorusMesh", "QuadMesh", "TextMesh", or "file" to load from a resource path

mesh_params.description: BoxMesh: {size:{x,y,z}}. SphereMesh: {radius,height,radial_segments,rings}. CylinderMesh: {top_radius,bottom_radius,height}. CapsuleMesh: {radius,height}. PlaneMesh: {size:{x,y}}. PrismMesh: {left_to_right,size:{x,y,z}}. TorusMesh: {inner_radius,outer_radius,rings}. QuadMesh: {size:{x,y}}. TextMesh: {text,font_size,depth}. file: {path:"res://mesh.tres"}

tool_description: Create and assign a material to a MeshInstance3D, CSG, or GeometryInstance3D node. Supports StandardMaterial3D or loading from file.

material_type.description: "StandardMaterial3D" or "file" to load from a resource path

material_params.description: StandardMaterial3D: {albedo_color:{r,g,b,a}, metallic:0-1, roughness:0-1, emission:{r,g,b}, emission_energy:float, transparency:0=disabled/1=alpha/2=scissor/3=hash/4=depth_pre_pass}. file: {path:"res://material.tres"}

surface_index.description: For MeshInstance3D only: surface index for per-surface override. Omit for material_override on all surfaces.

tool_description: Query computed 3D spatial data for a Node3D in a scene file. Returns local/global positions, scales, rotation quaternions, and subtree bounding boxes (AABB) when available. Use this before making precise 3D placement decisions.

node_path.description: Path to the Node3D (. for root, or relative path like Level/Props/Crate)

include_bounds.description: Include computed subtree AABBs when visual descendants exist (default: true)

tool_description: Measure the world-space distance between two Node3D nodes in a scene file. Returns both the full 3D delta and the horizontal XZ distance.
Snap a Node3D position to a grid in local or global space. Useful for modular level building and keeping 3D scenes aligned.

node_path.description: Path to the Node3D to snap

grid_size.description: Positive grid size. Use a number for uniform snapping or {x,y,z} for per-axis snapping.

axes.description: Axes to snap. Any of: ["x"], ["x","z"], ["x","y","z"] (default: all axes)

tool_description: Set MULTIPLE properties on a node in a single tool call. Non-atomic: each property is applied independently; the response separates "applied" from "failed" so partial success surfaces clearly. Saves the scene once at the end. Resource-typed properties must use set_resource_property / set_sprite_texture / etc.

node_path.description: Path to the node (. for root, or relative path)

properties.description: Map of property_name -> value. Each value follows the same form as modify_node_property.value (primitives, arrays, or {type:"Vector3",...} discriminated objects).

tool_description: Set, add, or remove a node's group memberships in a .tscn scene file. Groups persist to disk so the running game can call get_tree().get_nodes_in_group(name).

node_path.description: Path to the node (. for root)

groups.description: List of group names to apply

mode.description: replace (default): node ends up in EXACTLY the listed groups. add: union with existing. remove: drop the listed groups.

tool_description: Read the list of groups a node belongs to in a .tscn scene file.

Find every node in a .tscn that belongs to a given group. Returns paths, names, and types. Useful for verifying that level.gd will actually pick up the right nodes via get_tree().get_nodes_in_group().

group.description: Group name to search for

tool_description: Modify a property on a Resource that is currently held by a node (or by another resource attached to that node). Use this to tweak shape radii, material colors, gradient stops, etc., WITHOUT recreating the resource. resource_path walks from the node down to the resource using "/"-separated property names, e.g. "shape", "material", or "material/next_pass". After the change, saves the scene.

node_path.description: Path to the node owning the resource

resource_path.description: Path from node to the target resource via property names. Examples: "shape", "material", "material/next_pass"

property_name.description: Property on the target resource to set (e.g. "radius", "albedo_color")

tool_description: Save a Resource currently held by a node (or sub-resource) to a standalone .tres file so it can be referenced by other scenes / shared / committed. The node's property is then re-pointed to the loaded-from-disk version, so future set_resource_property calls write through to that file. Works for any Resource subclass: Material, Mesh, Shape, Curve, Gradient, etc.

resource_path.description: Path from node to the resource (e.g. "shape", "material")

tool_description:
Inspect ANY Godot Resource. Two modes:
  • path mode: pass {path: "res://foo.png"} for a resource on disk (.tres / .res / image / .glb / .ogg / .tscn / etc.)
  • node mode: pass {scene_path, node_path, resource_property} to inspect a resource attached to a node WITHOUT having to save it as .tres first (e.g. the shape on a CollisionShape2D, the material on a MeshInstance3D, the stream on an AudioStreamPlayer).
Returns class, file size (path mode), and type-specific info: width/height for textures, vertex/surface counts and AABB for meshes, length for AudioStream/Animation, node count for PackedScene, common Material properties, Shape extents, and the resource's dependencies.

path.description: Path mode: resource path on disk (res://...).

scene_path.description: Node mode: path to the .tscn that owns the node.

node_path.description: Node mode: path to the node within the scene.

resource_property.description: Node mode: property name on the node holding the resource (e.g. "shape", "material", "stream", "texture").

tool_description: List signal connections involving a node. source="scene_file" (default) reads connections persisted to a .tscn. source="runtime" requires the game to be running and reads live connections from the SceneTree. Use the runtime mode to verify dynamically-connected signals (those connected from code in _ready, not in the editor).

source.description: Where to read connections from. Default: scene_file

node_path.description: Path to the node. For source="runtime" use absolute (/root/Main/Player) or relative to current_scene.

include_outgoing.description: Include signals that this node emits (default: true)

include_incoming.description: Include signals from other nodes whose handler is on this node (default: true). Only honored for scene_file source.

tool_description: Connect a signal between two nodes inside a .tscn scene file. The target script must define the method (will refuse otherwise). Equivalent to clicking the "+" in the editor's Node > Signals panel and persists the connection to the .tscn. NOTE: scripts must be attached via attach_script (NOT via modify_node_property), otherwise the editor's in-memory node will not see the script and this tool will reject the connection.

signal.description: Signal name on the emitting node

method.description: Method name on the receiving node's script

tool_description: Remove a signal connection from a .tscn scene file. No-op if the connection doesn't exist.

Apply a SMALL, SURGICAL code edit (1-10 lines) to GDScript files. Auto-applies changes. For large changes, call multiple times. ONLY for .gd files - NEVER for .tscn scene files. Use classdb_query to verify unfamiliar Godot class methods. After making changes, consider using run_scene to test and get_errors to check for issues.

edit.description: Edit spec: {type: "snippet_replace", file: "res://path.gd", old_snippet: "old code", new_snippet: "new code", context_before: "line above", context_after: "line below"}. Keep old_snippet SMALL (1-10 lines).

tool_description: Validate a GDScript file for syntax errors using Godot's built-in parser. Call after creating or modifying scripts to ensure they are error-free.

path.description: Path to the GDScript file to validate (e.g., res://scripts/player.gd)

tool_description: Create a directory (with parent directories if needed).

path.description: Directory path (res://path/to/folder)

tool_description: Permanently delete a file from the project. REQUIRES confirm=true as an explicit safety gate — omitting confirm returns an error. Creates a .bak backup alongside the original by default (disable with create_backup=false). REFUSES if the file is currently open in the editor (any scene tab or script editor tab); close the tab first, or pass force=true to bypass the check (not recommended — deleting the active scene out from under the editor can crash Godot). Use ONLY when deletion is explicitly requested; NEVER as a way to "edit" or "reset" a file (use edit_script instead). Does not delete directories.

path.description: Path to the file to delete (e.g. res://scenes/old.tscn)

confirm.description: REQUIRED. Must be explicitly set to true — safety gate to prevent accidental deletes. Calls without confirm=true fail with an error.

create_backup.description: If true (default), saves a .bak copy next to the original before deletion so the file can be recovered. Set false to delete without backup.

force.description: If true, bypass the "file is open in editor" guard. Use ONLY if you know the file is not the active scene. The guard exists because deleting the active scene tab from under the editor can crash Godot.

tool_description: Rename or move a file, optionally updating references in other files.

update_references.description: Update references in other files (default: true)

tool_description: List all GDScript files in the project with basic metadata.
Concise project settings summary: main_scene, window size/stretch, physics tick rate, and render basics.

Return the full InputMap: built-in actions (ui_*, spatial_editor/*) plus all project-defined actions from project.godot. Each action maps to an object with "events" (array of key/mouse/gamepad bindings) and optionally "deadzone". Use this before configure_input_map to see current bindings and deadzones.

include_deadzones.description: Include the per-action "deadzone" field in each action object (default: true). When true, each action is {"deadzone": 0.5, "events": [...]}. When false, each action is {"events": [...]}.

tool_description: Return named 2D/3D physics collision layers from ProjectSettings.
Get available properties for a Godot node type. Use this to discover what properties exist on a node type (e.g., anchors_preset for Control, position for Node2D).
Return the latest lines from the Godot editor output log.

max_lines.description: Maximum number of lines to include (default: 50)

tool_description: Get errors and warnings from both the Godot Output panel and the Debugger > Errors tab. Returns file paths, line numbers, severity, stack traces, and which source each error came from. If errors mention a missing method or property, use classdb_query to verify the correct API before fixing.

max_errors.description: Maximum number of errors to return (default: 50)

include_warnings.description: Include warnings in addition to errors (default: true)

tool_description: Mark the current position in the Godot editor log. Subsequent get_console_log and get_errors calls will only return output after this point.
Open a file in the Godot editor at a specific line (side-effect only).

path.description: res:// path to open

tool_description: Dump the scene tree of the scene currently open in the Godot editor (node names, types, and attached scripts).

Browse Godot project settings by category. Returns values from the editor's in-memory state — this matches project.godot after a normal Godot save, but direct edits to project.godot on disk are not reflected until the editor restarts (rescan_filesystem does not help). Call without a category to see all available categories. Call with a category to see all settings with their current values, types, and valid options.

category.description: Settings category prefix (e.g., "display", "physics", "rendering", "application", "audio"). Omit to list all available categories.

tool_description: Update one or more Godot project settings. Pass a dictionary of setting paths to their new values. Use list_settings first to discover available setting paths, current values, and valid options for a category. For input action bindings, prefer configure_input_map — if you do pass input/* keys here, partial updates are merged safely (existing events are preserved).

settings.description: Dictionary of setting paths to new values (e.g., {"display/window/size/viewport_width": 1920, "display/window/size/viewport_height": 1080})

tool_description: Add, remove, or replace input actions and their key/button bindings. Use get_input_map to see current actions before modifying.

operation.description: "add" to create action and/or append events, "remove" to delete the action entirely, "set" to replace all events on an action (creates it if needed)

events.description: Input events to bind. Each object needs a "type" field: {"type":"key","key":"Space"} for keyboard, {"type":"mouse_button","button_index":1} for mouse (1=left,2=right,3=middle), {"type":"joypad_button","button_index":0} for gamepad, {"type":"joypad_motion","axis":0,"axis_value":1.0} for gamepad axis.

items.description: An input event descriptor with a "type" field and type-specific properties

tool_description: Launch a scene in the Godot editor. By default the call BLOCKS until the editor flips to playing state (so the next get_errors / take_screenshot / send_input call sees a real game). The response includes started, runtime_connected, wait_for_started_ms, wait_for_runtime_ms, scene_path, and runtime_root. Use runtime_root (e.g. "/root/Main") as the prefix for query_runtime_node node_path arguments — it is computed from the actual root node name in the .tscn, NOT from the file name. Set wait_for_runtime=true to additionally wait for the in-game MCPRuntime helper to connect (required before take_screenshot / send_input will work). Recommended testing loop: run_scene({wait_for_runtime:true}) → query_runtime_node / send_input / take_screenshot → get_errors → stop_scene.

scene.description: Scene to run: omit for main scene, "current" for the currently open scene, or a res:// path for a specific scene

block_until_started.description: Wait until the editor reports playing=true before returning (default: true). Up to startup_timeout_ms.

wait_for_runtime.description: Wait until the MCPRuntime in-game helper connects back (required for take_screenshot/send_input). Default: false.

startup_timeout_ms.description: Max time in ms to wait for the above signals. Default: 10000. Bump to 15000–20000 on slower machines or autoload-heavy projects.

tool_description: Stop the currently running scene in the Godot editor. Always stop the scene before editing code to avoid errors repeating every frame.
Compatibility shim: returns {playing, scene}. For richer info (uptime, runtime helper connectivity, last-launched target) prefer get_runtime_status.

Combined editor + runtime status snapshot. Returns playing, playing_scene, last_launched ("current"|"main"|res-path), uptime_ms since the most recent run_scene, and runtime_helper_connected (true once the in-game MCPRuntime autoload is talking to the MCP server).
Sleep server-side. Useful between input events to let the game process them. Capped at 30000ms / 30s. Pass either ms or seconds (ms wins if both given).

seconds.description: Seconds to wait (0.001..30). Convenient when the agent is thinking in seconds.

tool_description: Capture the current viewport of the running game and save it as a PNG. REQUIRES the game to be running with the MCPRuntime autoload connected (run_scene with wait_for_runtime=true first). Returns resource_path, absolute_path, width, height, and (optionally) base64_png. Default save location is res://addons/godot_mcp/cache/screenshots/.

save_to.description: Optional res:// or user:// destination path. Defaults to res://addons/godot_mcp/cache/screenshots/screenshot_<ms>.png

return_base64.description: Also include the PNG bytes inline as base64 (default: false). Useful when the agent has no filesystem access.

tool_description: Synthesize an InputEvent and dispatch it to the running game via Input.parse_input_event. REQUIRES the game to be running with the MCPRuntime autoload connected. Use this to drive automated tests: click buttons, press keys, fire input actions. For multi-step interactions, alternate send_input → wait → query_runtime_node / take_screenshot.

Query a live node in the running scene tree. REQUIRES the game to be running with the MCPRuntime autoload connected. Returns class, path, valid, groups, and a map of property values. By default returns position, global_position, rotation, scale, visible, modulate — pass `properties:["..."]` to override. Set include_children=true to also list direct child nodes.

node_path.description: Absolute path (e.g. /root/Main/Player) or relative to current_scene.

properties.description: Property names to read. Default: position, global_position, rotation, scale, visible, modulate.

include_children.description: List direct children {name, class}. Default: false.

include_groups.description: Include the node's group memberships. Default: true.

tool_description: Return entries from the MCPRuntime in-game ring buffer. The buffer holds the last ~500 lines pushed via MCPRuntime.push_runtime_log(level, text) from your scripts plus internal connection events. For full engine stdout (script prints, errors, warnings) use get_console_log — the editor already captures the running game's stdout. Returns entries with ts_ms, level, and text plus started_at_ms (when the helper started) and now_ms.

since_ms.description: Only return entries with ts_ms >= since_ms. Use 0 (default) for all.

tool_description: Query Godot's ClassDB for class information: properties, methods, signals, and inheritance. Use this to verify that a class, method, or property actually exists in the running Godot engine before writing code. Prevents using wrong method names, outdated Godot 3 API, or incorrect signatures.

include_virtual.description: Include well-known virtual methods like _ready, _process, _input (default: true). Set to false to see only public non-virtual methods.

tool_description: Trigger a full filesystem rescan in the Godot editor. Use after creating, deleting, or modifying files externally (e.g. from the terminal or another tool). The scan is asynchronous and returns immediately.
Register, unregister, or list autoload singletons. Autoloads are scripts/scenes loaded automatically at project start.

operation.description: "add" to register, "remove" to unregister, "list" to show all autoloads

path.description: res:// path to the script or scene file (required for "add")

tool_description: Render an SVG to a PNG asset on disk via Image.load_svg_from_buffer. The SVG is rendered directly from bytes — no temp file is created, so concurrent calls are safe and project-rename quirks (user:// rebinding) cannot break it. Returns resource_path, absolute_path, dimensions {width,height}, and the render_scale used.

svg_code.description: Complete SVG markup. Either single or double quotes are accepted in attributes.

filename.description: Output filename. ".png" appended if missing.

save_path.description: Destination directory (default: res://assets/generated/). Created if it does not exist.

width.description: Optional desired output width in pixels. Combined with the SVG's intrinsic width to derive a uniform render_scale.

height.description: Optional desired output height in pixels. Same as width but matched on the height axis. If both width and height are provided, width takes precedence for scale derivation.

scale.description: Optional explicit render scale (e.g. 2.0 = 2x). Overrides width/height-derived scaling. Default: 1.0.

tool_description: Crawl the entire Godot project and build an interactive visual map of all scripts showing their structure (variables, functions, signals), connections (extends, preloads, signal connections), and descriptions. Opens an interactive browser-based visualization.

root.description: Root path to start crawling from (default: res://)

include_addons.description: Whether to include scripts in the addons/ folder (default: false)

tool_description: Get the schema for an endpoint in the HIVE API. You can use the schema returned by this tool to call an endpoint with the `call_api_endpoint` tool.

endpoint.description: The name of the endpoint to get the schema for.

tool_description: call an endpoint in the HIVE API. Note: use the category endpoints to get the list of endpoints and `get_api_endpoint_schema` tool to get the schema for an endpoint.

endpoint_name.description: The name of the endpoint to call.

args.description: The arguments to pass to the endpoint. This must match the schema returned by the `get_api_endpoint_schema` tool.

tool_description: Get all endpoints in the "Market Data and Price" category. Endpoints to retrieve real-time and historical cryptocurrency prices, market caps, trading volumes, OHLC data, global market statistics, supported currencies, basic market performance metrics across different timeframes and asset platforms, stablecoin market analytics, stablecoin price tracking, comprehensive stablecoin market cap data across multiple chains, centralized exchange (CEX) trading data including real-time tickers, order books, recent trades, candlestick charts, best bid/ask prices, CEX exchange metadata and volume charts, derivatives pricing (index, mark, and premium), perpetual futures funding rates, leverage tiers, options trading analytics, and available trading markets/currencies across major exchanges. Provider guide: Use coingecko tools for market-wide price data. Use ccxt_ tools for CEX trading data. Use goldrush_ tools for on-chain token price history and gas prices across 100+ chains.

Get all endpoints in the "On-Chain DEX & Pool Analytics" category. Endpoints for analyzing on-chain decentralized exchange pools, liquidity data, trading pairs, DEX rankings, pool filtering, trending pools, OHLCV data for pools/tokens, trading volume analysis, comprehensive on-chain trading metrics across multiple networks and DEXs, real-time DEX trading analytics, advanced token trading intelligence with DEXScreener-style metrics, trader statistics (makers, buyers, sellers), aggregated trading data by tokens, volume breakdowns, trading activity analysis, DEX volume analytics across protocols and chains, and cross-chain bridge analytics.

Get all endpoints in the "Portfolio & Wallet" category. Endpoints for tracking user wallet balances, transaction history, portfolio positions across protocols and chains, net asset calculations, token holdings analysis, comprehensive wallet activity monitoring, real-time balance tracking, balance update history over time, multi-token portfolio analysis, balance changes with transaction context, financial auditing capabilities for individual users and addresses, wallet filtering and discovery, NFT holdings tracking, wallet PnL, DeFi positions, swap history, and wallet insight metrics. Provider guide: Use moralis_ tools for wallet intelligence (PnL, DeFi positions, swap history, net worth, approvals, active chains, wallet insights). Use goldrush_ tools for Bitcoin wallets, historical balance snapshots at specific blocks, 100+ chain coverage, and decoded transaction logs.

Get all endpoints in the "Token & Contract data" category. tool_description:
SINGLE session-start call — bundles auth state + external-tool detection (Clay / Crunchbase browser-cookie probes) + skill overrides + verbiflow browser-session probe into one response. Call this as the FIRST tool of every session before rendering anything to the user. Returns { auth, connected_tools, skill_overrides, browser: {verbiflow_signed_in} }.

`browser.verbiflow_signed_in` is a silent SQLite existence probe (no Keychain prompt) that detects whether the user is currently signed into *.verbiflow.com in any Chrome profile. Combine with auth.is_anonymous to decide whether the MCP session was lost vs. genuinely fresh:
  - is_anonymous=true AND verbiflow_signed_in=true → SUGGEST growth_relogin (strong signal: they have a real account, this MCP just lost its token).
  - is_anonymous=true AND verbiflow_signed_in=false → fresh anon user, route through normal claim flow at delivery (growth_claim_account_oauth).
  - is_anonymous=false → already authed, ignore the probe.

Report the current session: anonymous or claimed user, user_id, workspace slug, and the full list of workspaces the viewer belongs to (id, name, slug). Every skill flow should call this first. Use `workspaces` to name the destination when confirming sequence creation — and if length > 1, ask the user which workspace before calling growth_create_sequence_draft.

Nuke the MCP's local anon session and sign in fresh. Use when Supabase rejects the current tokens with "invalid JWT" / "signature invalid" — typically after a Supabase project JWT-key rotation. Creates a brand-new anonymous user; any previous unclaimed anon workspace is orphaned (Supabase sweeps them on its own schedule).

Preferred claim flow. Returns a one-click URL that hands this anonymous session to the browser and immediately starts Google (or Microsoft) OAuth. After sign-in, the OAuth identity attaches to the SAME user row, so the workspace / sequences / senders the MCP built carry over unchanged. Use this when the user needs to open the web builder or dashboard. Prefer this over growth_claim_account (magic-link) unless the user explicitly asks for email-based claim.

new_workspace_name.description: REQUIRED, non-empty. Display name for the new workspace — use the company name you researched the sequence for, e.g. "Acme Corp". The workspace is renamed to this on claim. Never pass an empty string.

new_workspace_domain.description: REQUIRED, non-empty. Company domain, e.g. "acme.com" — use the domain of the company you built the sequence for. The claim flow auto-enriches the workspace with the company logo, industry, and description (same as normal onboarding). Never pass an empty string.

tool_description: Attach an email to the current anonymous user. Supabase sends a magic link to the provided email; on click, the anonymous user becomes a real user with that email — workspace, sequences, and senders all carry over with no migration. Idempotent: already-claimed users get a fresh magic link. Returns a claim_token the agent can poll via growth_check_claim_status to detect when the user actually clicks the link.

Returns { status: "pending" | "claimed" | "expired", minted_at, claimed_at?, claimed_user_id?, claimed_email? }. Use this to wait for the user to finish OAuth or click their magic link without asking them to confirm. Poll roughly every 20-30s; stop on "claimed" or "expired".

tool_description:
Re-authenticate a user whose MCP session was previously real (claimed) but whose tokens got invalidated server-side (Supabase JWT key rotation, manual revoke, refresh window blown). Returns a one-click URL the user opens; the page does Google/Microsoft OAuth (not linkIdentity), grabs the resulting Supabase session for their EXISTING auth.users row, mints a per-user MCP token, and POSTs it to my local callback so auth.json recovers the same account — workspace, sequences, senders all reappear instantly.

WHEN to call: (a) the user explicitly asks to re-login / says they lost their session, OR (b) a tool call surfaced "Your session has expired or been invalidated by the server" and the current auth.is_anonymous=false (i.e. they HAD a real account before). NEVER call this for a fresh anonymous user who has never claimed — there's no prior account to re-bind to. For anonymous users use growth_claim_account_oauth (creates the account) or growth_claim_account (magic link) instead.

Different from growth_claim_account_oauth: claim is for anon → real conversion (uses linkIdentity, attaches OAuth to current anon user). Re-login is for already-real users who lost their tokens (uses signInWithOAuth, signs into the existing account).

tool_description:
Drive any site through the user's real Chrome. Opens a tab on `url` if no tab matching the host is already open (no-op when one exists — preserves user state), runs your `js` in it, then returns the post-state HTML and/or markdown plus your script's return value. Use for the long tail of public directories where a typed integration isn't worth it (AICPA peer review, FINRA broker check, NPI registry, state bar listings, FDA Orange Book, EDGAR, etc.).

**Standard scrape loop:** call once with empty `js` (`'return null'`) to get the landing-page HTML → inspect form/table structure → call again with `js` that ticks checkboxes / fills inputs / submits / waits for results → returns post-submit page.

**JS conventions:** wrap in `return` to get a value back. Async OK — `return await fetch(...)` is fine. The return value is JSON-stringified and surfaced in `js_result`. The JS is also where you'd run `await fetch(...)` if you want to hit the site's API directly (cookies, TLS, Cloudflare clearance all ride for free).

**Format param:** `'html'` (default — semantic, has form input names + hidden fields like `__VIEWSTATE`), `'markdown'` (cheaper for the agent to read; loses some semantic info), or `'both'`. Pick markdown when scanning content, html when you need selectors / form names / hidden inputs.

**`incognito: true`** opens the tab in a private window. Use for clean-session anonymous scrapes (no history, no cookies). **Tradeoff:** incognito drops the user's logged-in state, so any auth-walled site fails. Don't combine with sites you need to be signed into.

**Might-get-blocked warning:** if the site uses Cloudflare bot protection, hCaptcha / reCAPTCHA, an interstitial challenge, or sandboxed JS controllers (Pega, Salesforce, ServiceNow, etc.), JS injection may fail or trigger a block. Signs to look for in the response: `html` contains 'Just a moment', 'Access denied', 'cf-browser-verification', '<title>Attention Required'; `js_result` is empty when you expected data; navigation didn't actually fire after `.click()` (the page state didn't change). When that happens, escalate to `growth_chrome_applescript` for OS-level trusted input.

**Prereq (one-time):** Chrome > View > Developer > Allow JavaScript from Apple Events must be ON. The Crunchbase tools auto-flip this; otherwise tell the user to flip the menu item once.

**Same-origin only:** if your `js` does `fetch(otherOrigin)`, browser CORS applies. Open a tab on that origin first.

**Don't poke sensitive tabs uninvited.** If `host_match` could match `mail.google.com`, `slack.com`, `linkedin.com/messaging`, or any site where the agent could send/post/write on the user's behalf — confirm with the user first. Reading public directories needs no confirmation.

url.description: Absolute URL to open if no matching tab exists. Always required. Example: "https://peerreview.aicpa.org/public_file_search.html".

js.description: JavaScript to execute in the tab. Use `return ...` to surface a value via `js_result`. Pass `'return null'` to just snapshot the current page.

host_match.description: URL substring to match an existing tab. Defaults to the URL's host.

format.description: Default `html`. Pick `markdown` for cheap content scans, `html` when you need selectors / form names / hidden inputs, `both` when unsure.

incognito.description: Default false. Set true to open in a private window — clean session, no cookies, no history. Drops the user's logged-in state, so auth-walled sites fail. Use for anonymous public-directory scrapes.

tool_description:
Run raw AppleScript on the user's Mac. The escape hatch for cases where `growth_chrome_run`'s JS injection isn't enough — most often when a site's controllers gate on `event.isTrusted` and reject synthesized clicks (Pega web mashups, Salesforce Lightning, ServiceNow forms, some Cloudflare challenges). System Events sends real OS-level input that pages can't distinguish from the user.

**When to escalate from `growth_chrome_run` to this tool:**
- `.click()` and `dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click'))` don't trigger the action; UI state doesn't change.
- A page-internal global (Pega's `Grids`, etc.) isn't accessible from injected JS.
- You need to send a keystroke (Tab to focus, Enter to submit, ⌘+L to focus address bar, etc.).
- You need to interact with Chrome's own menus / dialogs (not the page DOM).

**Patterns:**
```applescript
-- Send keystroke to the focused Chrome window
tell application "Google Chrome" to activate
tell application "System Events" to keystroke tab
tell application "System Events" to key code 36  -- Enter

-- Click at screen coordinates (derive via JS first: getBoundingClientRect + window position)
tell application "System Events" to click at {x, y}

-- Run JS in a specific tab AND get the result back
tell application "Google Chrome"
  repeat with t in tabs of window 1
    if URL of t contains "aicpa.org" then
      return execute t javascript "document.querySelector('button.next').click()"
    end if
  end repeat
end tell
```

**Pagination loop pattern (Pega-style sandboxed grid):** focus the page → System Events keystroke Tab repeatedly to land focus on the 'Next' button → key code 36 (Enter) to trigger via real keypress → `growth_chrome_run` to scrape the new state → repeat. Or, derive button screen coordinates via `growth_chrome_run` (read `getBoundingClientRect`, add Chrome window's screen position via `tell application "Google Chrome" to bounds of window 1`), then System Events click at `{x, y}`.

**Returns** `{ stdout, stderr }` — AppleScript's last-expression value lands in stdout. Errors raise.

**Power + responsibility:** AppleScript has full machine access. It can quit apps, click anywhere on screen, send keystrokes to whatever window is focused (including `mail.google.com` if Gmail is up). Don't run scripts that could touch the user's other apps without explicit confirmation.

script.description: Raw AppleScript source. Multi-line OK. Last-expression value goes to stdout. To target Chrome specifically, wrap in `tell application "Google Chrome" ... end tell`. To send OS input, wrap in `tell application "System Events" ... end tell`.

tool_description:
Monkey-patch a tab's `fetch` + `XMLHttpRequest` to record every request the page makes — useful for reverse-engineering a site's AJAX endpoints. Once you see the actual URL + body the page sends, you can call it directly via `await fetch(...)` inside `growth_chrome_run` and skip pagination clicks entirely.

**Three actions:**
- `'start'` — install the observer in the matching tab. Idempotent (safe to call repeatedly). Optional `filter` substring restricts which requests get logged. Returns `{ js_result: 'started' | 'already_installed' }`.
- `'drain'` — return all entries collected since the last drain (or since start) AND clear the log. Returns `{ entries: [...] }` where each entry is `{ source: 'fetch' | 'xhr', method, url, status, request_body, response_body, started_at, duration_ms }`. Bodies are truncated to `max_body_chars` (default 8000) — bump for larger payloads. Pass `record_headers: true` on `start` to also capture `request_headers` + `response_headers` per entry — handy for reverse-engineering auth/CSRF flows (e.g. LinkedIn Voyager's `x-li-page-instance` + `x-li-track`).
- `'reset'` — clear the log without uninstalling the observer.

**Typical flow:** call `start` with a `filter` (e.g. `"/data/"`, `"api"`) → trigger an action in the page (click Next via `growth_chrome_run` or `growth_chrome_applescript`) → call `drain` to see what the page just fetched. Once you spot the endpoint + body shape, call it directly with `growth_chrome_run` (`await fetch(url, {...})`) — no more clicking.

**Limitation:** the observer survives page navigations within the same origin (no full reload). On a hard reload or a navigation to a different origin, re-call `start`. The patches are non-removable by design (no `stop` action) — they're cheap shims that the page will never notice.

url.description: Tab URL to attach the observer to (opens the tab if no matching tab exists).

action.description: What to do: `start` installs the observer (idempotent), `drain` returns + clears the log, `reset` clears the log without uninstalling.

host_match.description: URL substring to match the tab. Defaults to `url`'s host.

filter.description: Substring filter on request URL. Only requests whose URL contains this substring are logged. Empty string (default) logs everything. Use to cut noise — e.g. `"/data/"`, `"graphql"`, `"api.example.com"`.

max_body_chars.description: Max chars per request_body / response_body in the log. Default 8000. Bump if you need to capture larger payloads.

record_headers.description: Default false. When true, each entry also includes `request_headers` and `response_headers`. Set when reverse-engineering auth/CSRF flows.

tool_description: List Clay tables + workbooks the user has access to, using their local browser Clay session. macOS only. Workspace auto-discovered from the cookie unless `workspace_id` is pinned. Pass `query` to search by name (e.g. "fintech") — server-side filter, narrow + fast. Without `query`: returns up to 30 most-recently-opened tables. With `query`: returns ALL matches (no cap). Returns { tables: [{table_id, view_id, name, workbook_id, workbook_name, row_type, last_opened_at, workspace_id, workspace_name}, ...] }. `view_id` is often null in the list response — `growth_import_clay_table` resolves it lazily at import time. On mode: "unsupported", the user has no Clay session in that browser — ask them to log into Clay there, or try the other browser.

browser.description: Which browser the user is logged into Clay on.

query.description: Optional name filter. When set, server-side searches across ALL workbooks + tables in scope (uses isGlobalSearch). When omitted, returns the most-recently-opened items only.

workspace_id.description: OPTIONAL. Usually omit — workspaces are auto-discovered from the cookie. Pass only if the user explicitly names a specific workspace id.

tool_description: Export a specific Clay table as CSV using the user's local Clay session, then upload it to the named source node on a sequence draft (creates a staging session — same path the web CSV-upload flow uses). Use after growth_list_clay_tables / growth_parse_clay_table_url has identified the table_id + view_id the user picked. Requires an existing sequence draft with a source node (get source_node_id from growth_get_sequence). Returns { source_run_id, row_count, columns }. For arbitrary customer Clay tables, pass column_mapping when the columns are custom or ambiguous so staging/enrichment can use trusted canonical fields immediately. Surface the row_count to the user. macOS only (Clay cookie read).

browser.description: Which browser the user is logged into Clay on.

source_node_id.description: The source node id on the sequence draft to attach this CSV to.

ingress_id.description: Optional ingress id if the source node has multiple ingresses.

column_mapping.description: Optional explicit canonical mapping for customer-owned Clay tables. Use when the Clay table is arbitrary or has custom headers. Shape: {"contact_email":"Email","contact_linkedin_url":"LinkedIn Profile","company_domain":"Website"}. If omitted, only recognized aliases are mapped immediately and backend dynamic mapping may resolve the rest asynchronously.

tool_description: Parse a Clay table URL (the one the user sees in their browser tab when viewing a table) into its workspace_id / workbook_id / table_id / view_id components. Use this when the workspace has too many tables for growth_list_clay_tables to be useful, OR when the user just wants to use a specific table and has pasted its URL. Does NOT need the browser cookie — pure URL parsing.

url.description: Full Clay table URL, e.g. https://app.clay.com/workspaces/526097/workbooks/wb_X/tables/t_Y/views/gv_Z.

tool_description:
Run a Clay People Search using the user's own Clay account (browser session cookies). 

*** WHAT THIS IS: a PERSONA search — finds people who CURRENTLY hold a given title at companies matching firmographics (size / industry / location). Examples: "VPs of Servicing at mortgage companies 51-500 in the US", "DONs at hospice agencies", "Founders at YC W24 cos". 

*** WHAT THIS IS NOT: a HIRING SIGNAL search. If the user's play is "target companies actively hiring for {role}" (job_posting play, hiring-pain trigger), DO NOT use this tool — there is no live-job predicate here, just current title. Use the native `job_posting` audience source (Flage built-in, cleanest), or growth_search_clay_jobs to pull companies with live posts then chain into growth_find_people_at_companies for the right contacts. Confusing persona-search with hiring-signal is a recurring failure mode — read this carefully before picking. 

ASYNC. This call returns within seconds with `{ job_id, status: "running" }`. Clay searches take 4-8 min at typical scale (most of that is Clay streaming rows into the table — not anything we control). The actual work happens in the background; you MUST poll growth_clay_search_status({job_id}) every 15-30s to see progress and get the final CSV. Polling returns `current_rows` while streaming, then `result.csv_path` + sample + columns when complete. 

TWO MODES based on whether a sequence draft is passed: 

• DISCOVERY mode (no sequence_id + source_node_id) — pure search. When complete, status payload contains: { csv_path, sample, row_count, columns, company_domains, table_id, view_id, workbook_id }. Use when the user just wants to see the people (e.g. before committing to an audience, or when joining multiple searches). 

• ATTACH mode (both sequence_id AND source_node_id passed) — runs the search AND stages + promotes the rows as the sequence's audience. When complete, status payload also includes { source_run_id, promote_status, lead_list_id }. Requires an existing sequence draft. 

*** ALWAYS pass `filters.limit_per_company` (default: 5–10). Clay returns every contact that matches your filters — without a per- company cap, a single large company (e.g. JPMorgan in a financial- services search) floods the audience with dozens of contacts and crowds out the smaller companies that matter for the play. 5 for tight personas, 10 for broader ones. There is no global `limit` knob (intentionally — capping the total truncates the audience and hides whether filters are too narrow). 

Both modes save the CSV to $TMPDIR/flage-clay/ and register it in the manifest (growth_clay_list_saved_results). macOS only (Clay cookie read). If the user has multiple Clay workspaces, pass workspace_id explicitly.

sequence_id.description: Optional. Pass to ATTACH mode (stages + promotes rows as the sequence audience). Omit for DISCOVERY mode (pure search). If set, source_node_id is also required.

source_node_id.description: Optional. Required only if sequence_id is passed. Identifies which source node on the sequence draft to land the CSV on.

workspace_id.description: Clay workspace id. Optional — when omitted, auto-discovered from the cookie; errors if the user has more than one workspace.

workbook_name.description: Name for the NEW Clay workbook to create. Ignored if workbook_id is set.

workbook_id.description: Existing Clay workbook id (starts with wb_). When set, the new people table is created inside that workbook instead of creating a new one. Get workbook_id from growth_list_clay_tables — it's on every returned row.

table_name.description: Optional label for the table that gets created. Defaults to "Find people".

filters.description: Clay people-search filters. At least one must be non-empty (e.g. job_title_keywords, company_identifier, location_countries_include). See backend/flage/bridge/clay/payload.py for the full set.

job_title_seniority_levels.description: Allowed: intern, junior, associate, mid, senior, lead, manager, director, vp, cxo, founder, owner, partner, principal, staff.

job_functions.description: Allowed: engineering, product, design, marketing, sales, success, support, finance, hr, ops, legal, security, it, data, executive, growth, business.

company_identifier.description: Domains (or Clay-accepted company IDs) to seed the search from. Combine with start_from_method="CsvOfCompanies" to search people at specific companies.

company_industries_include.description: Exact Clay industry names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="industries") to get valid values.

company_industries_exclude.description: Exact Clay industry names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="industries") to get valid values.

location_countries_include.description: Exact country names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="countries") to get valid values.

headline_keywords.description: Substring match on the LinkedIn headline (the one-liner under the name). Combine with about_keywords and/or job_title_keywords to narrow further — e.g. job_title_keywords=["recruiter"] + headline_keywords=["hardware"] for hardware recruiters. AND-ed with the other filters; values within the array are OR-ed.

about_keywords.description: Substring match on the LinkedIn About section (long bio). Combine with headline_keywords and/or job_title_keywords to narrow — e.g. about_keywords=["hardware"] + headline_keywords=["hardware"] catches anyone who self-describes as hardware-focused. AND-ed with the other filters; values within the array are OR-ed.

profile_keywords.description: Substring match across the full LinkedIn profile text (broader than about/headline). Use when you want any mention anywhere in the profile, not just headline or bio.

limit_per_company.description: Cap on how many people Clay returns per company. DEFAULT: pass 5–10 (5 for tight personas, 10 for broader). Without this, one large company floods the result set and crowds out the smaller companies that matter for the play. This is the diversification knob — pass it on every call. (Note: there is no global `limit` knob — Clay returns every contact that matches the filters.)

tool_description:
Poll the status of a Clay search started via growth_search_clay_people, growth_search_clay_companies, or growth_search_clay_jobs. All three are async and return a `job_id`. Pass that `job_id` here. Returns: 
- `status`: "running" | "complete" | "failed" | "unknown" 
- `message`: short human-readable summary of the current step 
- `current_rows`: rows materialized in Clay so far (during streaming) 
- `log`: last ~40 progress lines with elapsed timestamps 
- `result`: populated when status="complete" — includes `csv_path`, `row_count`, `sample`, `columns`, `company_domains`, `table_id`, `view_id`, etc. For attach mode, also includes `source_run_id`, `promote_status`, `lead_list_id`. 
- `error`: populated when status="failed" 

Cadence: poll every 15-30 seconds while running. A typical search (10-50k rows) takes 4-8 min — most of which is Clay streaming rows. The fastest you can get the CSV is bound by Clay's upstream search throughput, not by polling frequency. Don't poll faster than every 10s — it adds load with no benefit. 

If status="unknown", the job_id never existed or its state was cleaned up (>7 days old). State persists across MCP-server restarts.

job_id.description: The job_id returned by growth_search_clay_people, growth_search_clay_companies, or growth_search_clay_jobs.

tool_description:
Export an EXISTING Clay table to a CSV on the local filesystem. No sequence required — the CSV path is returned for the model to read or pass into other tools (growth_join_clay_results_by_domain, growth_upload_clay_csv_to_sequence, etc.). 

Pass exactly ONE of the identifier args: 
- `table_id` (+ optional `view_id`; defaults to the table's firstViewId) 
- `table_url` (full Clay app URL — parsed for ids) 
- `job_id` (a previously-completed growth_search_clay_people job — the underlying table_id + view_id are read from the job state file) 
- `table_name` (substring; only works if exactly one table matches in the user's workspace — otherwise this errors with the candidates so the model can disambiguate) 

When to use this vs the other tools: 
- growth_search_clay_people / _companies / _jobs already write a CSV AND return its path — call this AFTER the fact only if you discarded the csv_path or the search completed in a previous conversation. 
- growth_import_clay_table attaches the CSV to a sequence audience — use that when the user wants the data in a sequence draft, not on disk. 

Returns the same shape as discovery-mode search: { csv_path, row_count, columns, sample, company_domains, table_id, view_id, workbook_id }. Typical runtime: 30-90s depending on row count (export + S3 download).

table_id.description: Clay table id (starts with t_). Pair with view_id for a non-default view.

view_id.description: Clay view id (starts with gv_). Optional — defaults to the table's firstViewId.

job_id.description: A previously-completed Clay search job id (clay_people_...). The table_id + view_id are read from the job's state file.

table_name.description: Substring match on table name. Resolved server-side; errors with candidates if more than one table matches.

tool_description:
Run a Clay Company Search (find-lists-of-companies) using the user's own Clay account (browser session cookies). DISCOVERY tool — does NOT stage rows to a sequence. 

ASYNC: returns a `job_id` immediately and runs the search in the background; you MUST poll growth_clay_search_status({job_id}) every 15-30s. When status="complete", the `result` field carries { csv_path, sample, company_domains, table_id, view_id, workbook_id, columns, row_count }. Feed company_domains into growth_search_clay_people's company_identifier[] to find contacts at these companies. 

BEST PRACTICE — semantic_description is the strongest single lever. Treat it like a concept prompt, not a keyword. When the user says "lead enrichment tools" or "find companies like Clearbit", DO NOT pass "lead enrichment" verbatim. Expand it into a rich 1-3 sentence description of what those companies actually do: what they sell, who they sell to, what their product category is called. Example: "B2B SaaS that enriches contact and company records with firmographic, technographic, and behavioral data. Typically sold to sales / marketing teams for prospecting and ABM. Comparable companies: Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Apollo, People Data Labs, Cognism." Clay's ranking is embedding-based — more specific concept text = better look-alikes. 

Combine semantic_description with structural filters (sizes, country_names, technographics_vendors, minimum_member_count) to narrow. locations / locations_exclude accept free-form strings (cities, states, regions) and DO NOT require a search_raw_location flag — that flag is people-search only. macOS only (cookie read).

workspace_id.description: Clay workspace id. Optional — auto-discovered when omitted.

workbook_name.description: Name for the NEW Clay workbook to create. Ignored if workbook_id is set.

workbook_id.description: Existing Clay workbook id (starts with wb_). When set, the new company table is created inside that workbook instead of creating a new one. Useful for chaining multiple searches (company + jobs + people) into the same workbook.

table_name.description: Optional label for the table. Defaults to "Find companies".

filters.description: Clay company-search filters. At least one must be non-empty. Common: semantic_description (free-text concept like "chip design"), industries[], country_names[], locations[] (free-form), sizes[], annual_revenues[], technographics_vendors[], minimum_member_count.

semantic_description.description: Free-text concept / theme — e.g. "chip design", "B2B SaaS payroll", "generative AI for legal".

industries.description: Exact Clay industry names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="industries") to get valid values.

industries_exclude.description: Exact Clay industry names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="industries") to get valid values.

country_names.description: Exact country names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="countries") to get valid values.

country_names_exclude.description: Exact country names — call growth_get_clay_enums(field="countries") to get valid values.

company_identifier.description: Optional seed domains. Empty + semantic_description = search all companies matching the concept.

tool_description:
Run a Clay Job-Posting Search (find-lists-of-jobs) using the user's own Clay account. DISCOVERY tool — does NOT stage rows to a sequence. 

ASYNC: returns a `job_id` immediately and runs the search in the background; you MUST poll growth_clay_search_status({job_id}) every 15-30s. When status="complete", the `result` field carries { csv_path, sample, row_count, columns, company_domains, table_id, workbook_id }. Typical use: find companies actively hiring for a role → pipe company_domains into growth_search_clay_people (with a job_title_keywords filter matching the persona) to reach the people doing that role at the hiring companies. 

USE THESE FILTERS (Clay's jobs output is reliable on them):
  - job_title_keywords — the primary signal. Substring match.
  - job_description_keywords — matches text in the posting body.
  - locations — free-form strings. Country (e.g. "United States"), state, metro, or city — Clay fuzzy-matches. Multiple values OR together.
  - min_num_days_since_posted / max_num_days_since_posted — recency window. Use max=30 for "posted in the last month".

AVOID THESE FILTERS (Clay's job data on these is noisy / inconsistent — results drop too aggressively):
  - employment_type (full-time/contract/etc.) — missing / mislabeled on many postings.
  - seniority — Clay infers this heuristically from the title and often gets it wrong. Rely on job_title_keywords instead (e.g. `["senior", "staff"]` or `["vp", "head of"]`).

There is no `limit` knob (intentionally — capping the count would truncate the audience and hide whether the filters are too narrow). Clay returns every matching job posting.

macOS only.

filters.description: Clay job-posting-search filters. At least one must be non-empty. Common: job_title_keywords, seniority, employment_type, min/max_num_days_since_posted, locations, company_identifier (seed list).

seniority.description: Free-form strings, lowercased. Clay silently drops unknown values.

company_identifier.description: Optional seed company domains to scope the search to.

tool_description: Join CSVs from a company search, people search, and/or jobs search on the canonical company_domain key (lowercased, www-stripped, path-stripped). Reads the csv_path returned by each growth_search_clay_* call, joins row-by-row on normalized company_domain, writes a merged summary CSV (one row per domain with aggregated people/jobs counts + first-N samples) and a detail JSON file (full nested structure), and returns { csv_path, json_path, row_count, sample, counts }. Use after running 2+ of the growth_search_clay_* tools to see which companies appear across multiple searches (e.g. "which chip-design companies are ALSO hiring security guards?"). Pure client-side — no Clay API calls, no extra credits.

companies_csv_path.description: Path returned in the `csv_path` field of a prior growth_search_clay_companies call. Typically /tmp/flage-clay/company-t_xxx-<ts>.csv.

people_csv_path.description: Path returned in the `csv_path` field of a prior growth_search_clay_people call (people search also writes its CSV to tmp alongside the staged audience).

jobs_csv_path.description: Path returned in the `csv_path` field of a prior growth_search_clay_jobs call.

tool_description: List every Clay CSV / JSON saved locally in this session by growth_search_clay_* and growth_join_clay_results_by_domain. Returns a manifest of { path, kind, entity_kind, label, row_count, table_id, workbook_id, saved_at } so the LLM can recall what's on disk without re-running searches. Use when the user asks "what do I have so far?" or when building a join and needing to find the paths of earlier search results. Pure filesystem read — no Clay or backend calls.

kind.description: Filter to a single kind. Omit to return all saved artifacts.

entity_kind.description: Filter to a single entity kind. Omit to return all.

tool_description:
Stage a CSV file (from ANY source — Clay searches, the join output, a user-provided path, etc.) onto a sequence draft as its audience. Reads csv_path from disk, validates the headers, then runs the same staging + promotion path used by growth_import_clay_table and the web CSV-upload flow. Returns { source_run_id, row_count, columns, promote_status, lead_list_id, column_mapping }. 

VALIDATION — this tool REQUIRES the CSV to have at least one contact identifier column: an email column (email, email_address) OR a LinkedIn URL column (linkedin_url, linkedin_profile, profile_url, etc.). Without one of those, Flage has no way to reach the contacts. The LLM should verify this BEFORE calling the tool — inspect the `columns` field returned by the search tool (or read the CSV header with a file tool) and confirm the user's CSV has email or linkedin_url. If it doesn't, surface the issue instead of calling this — company-only or job-posting CSVs cannot be staged as an audience; they need to be chained through a people search first. 

Use after growth_search_clay_people (discovery mode), growth_join_clay_results_by_domain (if the join CSV has contact columns), or any user-provided CSV on disk. NOT needed when growth_search_clay_people is called in ATTACH mode (sequence_id + source_node_id passed) — that path already stages.

csv_path.description: Absolute path to the CSV to upload. Typically the csv_path from a prior growth_search_clay_* / growth_join_clay_results_by_domain call, but can be any CSV the user points at.

source_node_id.description: Source node on the sequence draft to attach the CSV to.

ingress_id.description: Optional ingress id if the source node has multiple ingresses.

list_label.description: Human-readable label shown on the lead list in the builder UI. Defaults to "CSV · {filename}".

file_label.description: Filename label used by the staging endpoint. Defaults to the CSV's basename (without .csv suffix).

column_mapping.description: Explicit target mapping for generic/user CSVs when headers are not already canonical or recognized aliases. Shape: {"contact_email":"Email Address","contact_linkedin_url":"LinkedIn","company_domain":"Website"}. Values may also be full objects: {"contact_email":{"source_column_name":"Email Address","category":"contact_identifier","label":"Email"}}. Accepted categories are contact_identifier, company_identifier, contact_enrichment, company_enrichment. Use canonical target keys such as contact_email, contact_linkedin_url, contact_full_name, contact_first_name, contact_last_name, contact_job_title, company_name, company_domain, company_website, company_linkedin_url, company_description. Unmapped raw columns remain source_row/display data and are not promoted as resolver-trusted enrichment fields. Agents should pass this for non-Clay/user CSVs with custom headers instead of relying on raw header names.

tool_description:
Check whether a CSV has values for the template variables ({{first_name}}, {{company_name}}, etc.) used in a sequence's message copy. Call this BEFORE growth_upload_csv_to_sequence so you can warn the user (or pick a different CSV / enrich first) when too many leads are missing fields. 

Pass `variables` as the list extracted from the copy — strip the curly braces, e.g. ["first_name", "company_name", "job_title"]. Returns { total_leads, per_variable_coverage, leads_with_missing, all_have_required, summary }. `per_variable_coverage` gives missing_count + missing_percent per variable; `leads_with_missing` lists row indices + identifier + the variables they lack so you can show the user concrete examples.

csv_path.description: Absolute path to the CSV to check.

variables.description: List of template variable names (without {{}}) used in the sequence copy. Inspect the message body / subject / connection note / linkedin message and pull every {{var}}. Sender variables (sender_name, sender_first_name, sender_email, sender_title) are ignored — they come from the sender.

column_mapping.description: Optional explicit mapping from canonical field key → CSV column header, same shape as growth_upload_csv_to_sequence.column_mapping. Use when CSV headers are ambiguous.

sample_size.description: Cap on how many bad-lead examples to return in leads_with_missing (default 20). Coverage stats always cover the full CSV.

tool_description: Look up valid Clay filter values for a given field. Use this before constructing search filters to get exact string values that Clay accepts. Supports optional keyword search to narrow a large list (e.g. search "software" in industries). Returns the field type, which tools/filters it applies to, total count, and the matching values. Fields: "industries" (applies to company + people industry filters), "countries" (applies to country_names and location_countries_include).

field.description: Which enum field to look up.

search.description: Optional keyword to filter the list (case-insensitive substring match). Omit to get all values.

tool_description:
Join two CSV files on a shared column and write the merged result to disk. Pure local operation — no network, no browser session. Default is a LEFT JOIN: every row from the left CSV is kept; matching columns from the right CSV are appended. Use this whenever you have two CSVs about the same entities (e.g. a people CSV with company_linkedin_url + a companies CSV with company_linkedin_url + company_domain + company_name) and you want a single CSV with all the columns. 

Pass `on` when both sides share the same column name; pass `left_on` + `right_on` when the names differ. `normalize_key` handles common normalization gotchas: "linkedin_url" strips /about/, trailing slashes, query strings, and lowercases; "domain" strips https://, www., paths; "lowercase" just lowercases; "none" matches as-is. 

Returns { csv_path, matched_rows, unmatched_left, unmatched_right, columns } so you can immediately see how clean the join was.

left_csv_path.description: Absolute path to the LEFT CSV (the side whose rows are kept under the default left-join). Typically the larger / row-level file (e.g. people).

right_csv_path.description: Absolute path to the RIGHT CSV (the side providing extra columns to merge in). Typically the smaller / lookup-style file (e.g. companies).

on.description: Join column name (must exist on both sides). Use this OR `left_on`+`right_on`.

left_on.description: Join column name on the LEFT CSV. Only needed when column names differ.

right_on.description: Join column name on the RIGHT CSV. Only needed when column names differ.

how.description: Default "left". inner = drop unmatched on both sides. left = keep all left rows. right = keep all right rows. outer = keep everything.

normalize_key.description: How to normalize the join key before matching. Default "lowercase". Use "linkedin_url" for company LinkedIn URLs (strips /about/, trailing slashes, query strings), "domain" for hostnames (strips https://, www., paths).

output_label.description: Optional label for the output filename. Default "joined".

tool_description: Returns the available data source options for a given play, filtered by which tools the user has connected. Call this immediately after the user confirms the play + channel_mix, BEFORE any search. If needs_user_choice is true, show the options and ask the user to pick. If false, proceed silently with the single option returned. Always surface CSV upload as an additional fallback regardless of the result.

play.description: The play kind the user confirmed. Use one of: "hiring_signal", "persona_search", "post_reactors", "incubator", "recently_funded", "same_investor_portfolio", "company_search". Pass the closest match — the tool returns an empty options list for unknown plays.

connected_tools.description: Tool names the user has connected (from growth_session_init connected_tools where present=true). E.g. ["clay", "crunchbase"]. Pass an empty array if none are connected.

tool_description: Deeply research a company by domain — scrapes their homepage for hero copy / customer logos / testimonials, resolves their LinkedIn company page, finds founders, and pulls the last 5 posts from each founder + the company page. Cached 30 days per domain. Blocks up to ~45s for a fresh run; if it's still not done, returns status "running" with a workflow_id so the skill can tell the user to hold on. ALWAYS confirm with the user before calling this tool (never mention cost/credits/quotas to the user — onboarding is free for them).

force.description: Re-run even if a fresh cached result exists. Default false.

wait_seconds.description: How long to poll before returning a running status. Default 45.

tool_description: Return the latest stored company-research payload for a domain, without waiting. Use when the user returns after a long gap and you want to check whether a previously-kicked-off workflow has completed since.

Given a VC firm name (e.g. "Sequoia Capital", "Andreessen Horowitz", "Y Combinator"), return the list of companies they've publicly invested in by scraping the firm's own portfolio page. Used by the "same-investor warm intro" play (see ~/.claude/skills/growth/playbook.md) to build a target list of other companies backed by the user's own investors. Cached 90 days per investor. Confirm with the user before calling (never mention cost/credits — onboarding is free for them).

investor_name.description: The VC firm name. Can be the short form ("a16z", "YC") or the full name ("Andreessen Horowitz", "Y Combinator").

tool_description:
Bulk-enrich a list of LinkedIn company URLs with firmographic data (name, employee count, industry, HQ, founded year, description). Lightweight wrapper around the company-enrichment pipeline — pick the exact fields you want from the enrichments enum, and the response only contains those fields. Up to 25 URLs per call; sync, completes in 30-90s for typical batches.

INPUT IS LINKEDIN URLS ONLY. If you have domains, call growth_resolve_company_linkedin_urls first to convert them.

Common use: confirming target company size before locking an audience (e.g. "the Clay job search returned Google + Uber alongside real targets — pull employee_count_band on the top 25 to see how many are sub-150-emp"). NEVER auto-filter by size silently — surface the result to the user and let them decide whether the big-co names belong.

linkedin_urls.description: LinkedIn company / school URLs (e.g. "https://linkedin.com/company/anthropic"). Pass plain URLs — the backend normalizes /about and trailing slashes.

enrichments.description: Exact fields to return per company. `employee_count_band` is the LinkedIn size string ("11-50 employees", "1,001-5,000 employees", etc.) — best for size-band smell tests. `employee_count` is the numeric value when available. `industries` is an array. `headquarters` is a free-form string (e.g. "San Francisco, California"). Keep the list short — unrequested fields are dropped, no over-fetch.

tool_description: Force the user's workspace subscription to re-sync its per-product quantities (email mailboxes, LinkedIn accounts, etc.) against the actual count of connected senders. Call this AFTER the user confirms a Stripe checkout completed, so seats created via MCP pre-payment get billed on the fresh subscription. Also safe to call any time the user reports a billing mismatch ("I connected LinkedIn but it's not on my invoice"). Idempotent and fast — no-op on orgs with no subscription.

Create a real, persistent LinkedIn sender in the user's workspace by reading the user's active LinkedIn session from their local browser. REQUIRES the `browser` arg: "chrome" or "safari" — ask the user which browser they're logged into LinkedIn on before calling this. In gateway mode the configured GROWTH_MCP_BROWSER_PROVIDER is used instead so the cookie read stays inside the scoped gateway browser identity. No extension, no platform visit. The backend connects the account through Unipile and derives the display name + profile URL from the account metadata. Use this when growth_list_senders shows has_linkedin_account === false AND the user has consented to pulling their local LinkedIn session. macOS/Windows only — returns { mode: "unsupported" } elsewhere; skill should fall back to the senders_url flow. Safari extraction requires Claude Code to have Full Disk Access (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access); if the user picks Safari and the call fails with a permissions error, instruct them to grant FDA + restart Claude Code, then retry.

browser.description: Which browser the user is currently logged into LinkedIn on. Required on macOS. Windows only supports "chrome".

chrome_profile.description: Optional Chrome profile name when browser="chrome" (default: "Default").

sender_id.description: Optional. When set, the LinkedIn account is attached to this existing sender instead of creating a new one — use this whenever growth_list_senders returned a sender for this user, so they don't end up with duplicate sender rows (one for email, one for LinkedIn). Omit only for a truly fresh workspace where the LinkedIn connect is the first sender creation.

tool_description: Create a new sender (the identity that does the sending) in the user's workspace. Call this ONLY when growth_list_senders returned an empty array AND the user has given you their first name, last name, and (optionally) email. This is the FIRST step of onboarding a net-new user — it makes a sender row they can then attach a mailbox or LinkedIn account to. After this returns, immediately follow up with one of: growth_connect_linkedin_from_cookies, growth_connect_mailbox_oauth, or growth_connect_mailbox_app_password — do NOT leave the user with a sender that has no channel connected. Returns { sender_id, display_name, primary_email, ... }.

primary_email.description: The sender's primary email address. Optional but strongly recommended — pass it whenever the user has given it; it's used for display + as a default identifier when connecting a mailbox.

display_name.description: Optional display override. When omitted, the backend derives it from first + last name.

tool_description: Move a single sender_account (mailbox or LinkedIn) from one sender to another within the same workspace. The canonical use-case: merge two duplicate senders for the same human — e.g. the email connect created one sender and an earlier LinkedIn connect created a second — by moving the account from the duplicate onto the primary sender, then deleting the now-empty duplicate. Reversible: call again with the original sender_id to move it back. Doesn't recreate anything, just repoints `sender_accounts.sender_id`. Call growth_list_senders first to pick the `sender_account_id` of the account to move and the `target_sender_id` of the sender to move it onto.

sender_account_id.description: The sender_account_id to move (from growth_list_senders → senders[].accounts[].sender_account_id).

target_sender_id.description: The sender_id to move the account onto (from growth_list_senders → senders[].sender_id).

tool_description: Quote the cost of the next Gmail / Microsoft OAuth mailbox connect for this workspace. Call this RIGHT BEFORE asking the user 'OAuth or app password?" so you can tell them how many free OAuth mailboxes they have left vs. how much the next one will cost. Returns { current_count, free_quota, will_be_charged, price_cents, requires_workspace_subscription, has_workspace_subscription }. Rule of thumb wording: if `will_be_charged === false` → *"OAuth: free, you've used {current_count} of {free_quota} free mailboxes."*. If `will_be_charged === true` → *"OAuth: the next mailbox is ${price_cents/100}/mo (you've already used your {free_quota} free ones)."*. App password is always free regardless — mention that in the same breath so the user can make an informed pick.

Generate a Unipile hosted-OAuth link the user clicks to connect a Gmail or Microsoft mailbox to an existing sender. Returns { auth_url, provider_link_id, will_be_charged, price_cents }.
